module_title: Mughal Empire - Administration, Economy, and Culture
introduction: This level focuses on the robust administrative mechanisms, the land revenue system, and the cultural zenith achieved by the Mughals. Akbar's 'Mansabdari' system was the backbone of Mughal administration. Significant advancements were also made in literature, painting, and architecture.

core_concepts.title: Mansabdari System
core_concepts.description: Introduced by Akbar, this was a unique military and civil administrative system. 'Mansab' means rank. It consisted of two numbers: 'Zat' (personal rank/salary) and 'Sawar' (number of cavalrymen to maintain).

core_concepts.title: Dahsala / Zabti System
core_concepts.description: Akbar's finance minister, Todar Mal, introduced this land revenue system. Tax was fixed at 1/3rd of the average yield based on the production and prices of the previous 10 years.

core_concepts.title: Literature and Translation
core_concepts.description: Persian was the court language. Akbar established a translation department (Maktab Khana). The Mahabharata was translated into Persian as the 'Razmnama' (Book of Wars).

core_concepts.title: Mughal Painting
core_concepts.description: Humayun brought Persian painters to India, but Mughal painting reached its peak under Jahangir. The focus shifted to naturalism, flora, fauna, and portraiture.

core_concepts.title: Architectural Marvels
core_concepts.description: Key structures include Humayun's Tomb (first double dome and precursor to Taj Mahal), Fatehpur Sikri (Akbar's new capital), and the Taj Mahal (extensive use of Pietra Dura inlay technique).

important_entities.name: Todar Mal
important_entities.significance: Architect of the Ain-i-Dahsala (revenue system). He had previously served under Sher Shah Suri.

important_entities.name: Abul Fazl
important_entities.significance: Authored the 'Akbarnama' and 'Ain-i-Akbari', the most detailed contemporary accounts of Akbar's reign.

important_entities.name: Nur Jahan
important_entities.significance: Highly powerful in Mughal politics (formed the Nur Jahan 'Junta'). She built the tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah, which features the first large-scale use of Pietra Dura.

important_entities.name: Ustad Mansur
important_entities.significance: Specialized in depicting plants and animals (e.g., the famous painting of the Siberian Crane).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often assume titles were passed down to sons. In reality, upon a Mansabdar's death, his rank and property reverted to the Emperor (the law of Escheat).
Not all Mansabdars received cash. Those who received land assignments (the right to collect revenue) in lieu of salary were specifically called 'Jagirdars'.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: B-Birbal, A-Abul Fazl, T-Tansen, B-Bhagwan Das, A-Abdur Rahim, T-Todar Mal, M-Man Singh, D-Mulla Do Pyaza, H-Hakim Hukam.
Jahangir (Golden Age of Painting), Shah Jahan (Golden Age of Architecture).

exam_strategy_tips: Memorize the list of important books and their authors (e.g., Tuzuk-i-Baburi by Babur, Humayun-nama by Gulbadan Begum).
Questions testing the meaning of administrative terminology (e.g., Diwan, Mir Bakhshi, Sadr-us-Sudur) are frequently asked.
